question: On Marvell Technology's fiscal second-quarter 2027 earnings call (August 27, 2026; Marvell's fiscal 2027 ends in late January 2027), what did the CFO say about (a) the amount of capacity prepayments to suppliers expected in fiscal 2027, (b) expected fiscal 2027 non-GAAP operating expenses and how that compared with the prior expectation, and (c) when non-GAAP operating margin was expected to enter its 38%-40% long-term target range?
company: Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL, Nasdaq; fiscal year ends on the Saturday nearest January 31; fiscal 2027 ends January 30, 2027)
failure_mode: Marvell's release (8-K Ex. 99.1) gives only Q3 guidance (revenue $3.150B +/-5%, non-GAAP opex about $655M, EPS) and its slide deck adds FY27 (~$12B) and FY28 (~$18B) revenue outlook, but neither states the ~$1B supplier prepayments, the ~$2.55B FY27 non-GAAP opex (vs prior $2.45B) or the Q4 FY27 timing for the 38%-40% margin range. Traps: giving the Q3 opex (~$655M) as the full-year figure, giving the superseded $2.45B, treating fiscal 2027 as calendar 2027, using the reset long-term model expected at the October 6, 2026 investor day (after the as_of date), or using the revenue outlook that is on the slides.
expected_source: Marvell Q2 FY2027 earnings call transcript (CFO Dan Durn prepared remarks), August 27, 2026; absence checked in the 8-K press release and slide deck.
grading: Key points (all required): (a) approximately $1 billion of capacity prepayments to suppliers in fiscal 2027; (b) fiscal 2027 non-GAAP operating expenses of approximately $2.55 billion, slightly ABOVE the prior expectation of $2.45 billion; (c) non-GAAP operating margin likely to enter the 38%-40% long-term target range in Q4 of fiscal 2027 (the quarter ending about January 30, 2027). Accept 'about/roughly'; tolerance +/-$0.05B on opex. Fail if the answer gives $655M (Q3 guide) or $2.45B as the current full-year opex, places the margin milestone in calendar 2026/2027 without tying it to Q4 FY27, or cites targets announced at the October 6, 2026 investor day.
why_analysts_ask: Opex trajectory, supplier prepayments (cash-flow drag) and margin timing determine Marvell's FY27-FY28 earnings and free-cash-flow models, and none is in the press release.
answer: (a) About $1 billion of capacity prepayments to suppliers in fiscal 2027 ('we remain on pace'); (b) fiscal 2027 non-GAAP opex of approximately $2.55 billion, slightly above the prior $2.45 billion; (c) non-GAAP operating margin likely to enter the 38%-40% long-term target range in Q4 of fiscal 2027 [W03-E1, W03-E2]. The press release has only Q3 guidance (non-GAAP opex ~$655M) and the deck has revenue outlook but none of these three items [W03-E3, W03-E4].

question: Jabil (fiscal year ends August 31) reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results and its fiscal 2027 outlook on September 30, 2026. Combine the fiscal 2027 outlook figures in the press release (net revenue, core operating margin, core diluted EPS) with the core tax rate and net interest expense management gave on the earnings call, and compute the diluted share count implied for fiscal 2027. Assume core earnings = (core operating income - net interest expense) x (1 - core tax rate), use the midpoint of any range, and ignore other income/expense.
company: Jabil Inc. (JBL, NYSE; fiscal year ends August 31; fiscal 2027 = September 2026-August 2027)
failure_mode: The tax rate (20%) and net interest expense ($390-400M for FY27; ~$95M for Q1) were given only on the call: they are absent from the press release and (per a secondary summary of the slides) from the slide deck. Needs two sources (release for revenue/margin/EPS; call for tax and interest). Traps: using GAAP tax rates, using the Q1 interest figure ($95M) for the full year, using Q4 FY26 core EPS ($4.40) instead of the FY27 $17.55, treating 6.1% as GAAP margin, or computing shares from FY26 data.
expected_source: Jabil Q4 FY2026 press release (Sept 30, 2026) for revenue/margin/EPS; earnings call transcript (CFO Greg Hebard) for core tax rate and net interest expense.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) identifies the call-only inputs: core tax rate 20% and FY27 net interest expense of $390-$400 million; (2) core operating income = 6.1% x $44.5B = about $2.71B; (3) implied diluted shares about 105.7 million (accept 105.0-106.5 million; arithmetic: (2,714.5 - 395) x 0.80 / 17.55). Fail if the tax rate or interest expense is not the call figure, if the result is outside 104-107 million, or if the answer omits the units. A bonus consistency check (not required): Q4 FY26 diluted weighted-average shares were 106.0 million.
why_analysts_ask: Bridging revenue and margin guidance to EPS requires the tax and interest assumptions that EMS companies only give on the call, and the implied share count shows how much buyback is embedded in the guide.
answer: About 105.7 million diluted shares. Core operating income = 6.1% x $44,500M = $2,714.5M [W04-E3]; the CFO said the core tax rate is expected to be 20% for Q1 and the fiscal year and net interest expense about $95M for Q1 and $390-$400M for the full year [W04-E1, W04-E2]; ($2,714.5M - $395M) x (1 - 0.20) = $1,855.6M core earnings; divided by $17.55 core EPS [W04-E3] = about 105.7M shares (105.5-106.0M across the interest range), consistent with 106.0M diluted weighted-average shares in Q4 FY26 [W04-E3]. The press release gives no tax rate or interest-expense outlook [W04-E3].

question: In the NHTSA safety recall campaign 26V495 filed by Chrysler (FCA US LLC, part of Stellantis) in July-August 2026 for Ram 1500 pickups, how many U.S. vehicles are potentially affected, which model years are covered, what is the defect, and when were owner notification letters expected to be mailed?
company: Stellantis N.V. (STLA, NYSE/Euronext Milan/Euronext Paris; files 20-F; fiscal year ends December 31); recall filed by FCA US LLC (Chrysler/Ram)
failure_mode: Scope trap: the NHTSA figure is U.S. only (1,271,294 vehicles); some press coverage cites 'just over 1.5 million' worldwide (including Canada, Mexico and other markets). The manufacturer report date (30 July 2026) differs from the NHTSA acknowledgement letter date (3 August 2026). No financial charge was disclosed.
expected_source: NHTSA recall acknowledgement letter for campaign 26V495 (3 August 2026); press coverage for worldwide count.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) potential number of units affected in the U.S. = 1,271,294 (accept 'about 1.27 million'); (2) model years 2019-2026 Ram 1500; (3) defect = second-row seat belt buckle anchors (second-row center or driver side) may have been improperly installed/attached to the body structure, failing FMVSS 210 'Seat Belt Assembly Anchorages'; (4) owner notification letters expected to be mailed on 18 August 2026. Optional: manufacturer report date 30 July 2026; free remedy by dealers; ~1.5 million worldwide. Fail if the answer gives 1.5 million as the NHTSA/U.S. count, gives other model years, or cites a different campaign.
why_analysts_ask: Recall volume and defect type drive warranty-accrual and reputation questions for Stellantis's most profitable North American product.
answer: NHTSA campaign 26V495 (Chrysler/FCA US LLC; manufacturer report date 30 July 2026, NHTSA letter 3 August 2026) covers a potential 1,271,294 U.S. vehicles: 2019-2026 Ram 1500 pickups whose second-row seat belt buckle anchors may have been improperly installed, so they fail to comply with FMVSS 210; dealers inspect and attach the anchors free of charge and owner notification letters were expected to be mailed on 18 August 2026 [W08-E1]. Press coverage puts the worldwide total at just over 1.5 million (about 156,000 Canada, 15,000 Mexico, 75,000 elsewhere) [W08-E2].

question: What did Samsung Electronics report as consolidated revenue and operating profit for the second quarter of 2026 (April-June 2026) in its final results, in Korean won, and what was the operating margin of its DS (Device Solutions) division? Samsung had issued preliminary earnings guidance earlier in July.
company: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. (005930.KS, Korea Exchange; not registered with the SEC; fiscal year ends December 31; reports in KRW, K-IFRS)
failure_mode: Preliminary vs final: Samsung's 7 July 2026 guidance (about KRW 171 trillion revenue, about KRW 89.4 trillion operating profit, range 89.3-89.5 trillion) is superseded by the 30 July final figures (KRW 171.5 trillion; KRW 89.5 trillion). Division trap: the DS division (memory/foundry/System LSI) earned KRW 89.2 trillion of the KRW 89.5 trillion total, while MX/Networks lost KRW 0.7 trillion; the DS margin must be computed on DS revenue (KRW 127.5 trillion), not on consolidated revenue. Currency/unit trap: figures are in trillions of won, not dollars; Samsung does not file with the SEC, so the source is its own release.
expected_source: Samsung Electronics Q2 2026 results release (30 July 2026) and earnings guidance release (7 July 2026), on Samsung's newsroom.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) final Q2 2026 consolidated revenue KRW 171.5 trillion; (2) final consolidated operating profit KRW 89.5 trillion (accept 89.4-89.6 only if identified as the final result - 89.4 trillion is the preliminary July 7 estimate); (3) DS division revenue KRW 127.5 trillion and operating profit KRW 89.2 trillion, giving an operating margin of about 70.0% (accept 69.5%-70.5%). Optional: MX/Networks revenue KRW 33.2 trillion with an operating loss of KRW 0.7 trillion; DS = about 99.7% of consolidated operating profit. Fail if the DS margin is computed on consolidated revenue (52%), if the preliminary 89.4 trillion is presented as the final figure, or if USD figures are given instead of won.
why_analysts_ask: Samsung's record quarter is almost entirely a memory (DS) story, so analysts split consolidated profit by division and track preliminary-versus-final revisions.
answer: Final Q2 2026 (released 30 July 2026): consolidated revenue KRW 171.5 trillion and operating profit KRW 89.5 trillion (the 7 July preliminary guidance had been about KRW 171 trillion and about KRW 89.4 trillion). The DS division had revenue of KRW 127.5 trillion and operating profit of KRW 89.2 trillion, an operating margin of about 70.0% (89.2/127.5), i.e. roughly 99.7% of consolidated operating profit; MX/Networks posted revenue of KRW 33.2 trillion and an operating loss of KRW 0.7 trillion [W09-E1, W09-E2, W09-E3].

question: In September 2026 Copart agreed to acquire ACV Auctions. As of 3 October 2026, using the cash price per share and the implied equity value Copart announced, and ACV's reported revenue, what multiple of ACV's trailing-twelve-month (TTM) revenue for the twelve months ended June 30, 2026 does the implied equity value represent? failure_mode: Two-source calculation: deal terms come from Copart's 10 September 2026 announcement (US$10.50 per share, all cash by tender offer then merger, implied equity value about US$1.9 billion, about 45% premium to the 10 August 2026 unaffected close, close expected by year-end 2026); revenue comes from ACV's Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 earnings releases. Traps: using FY2025 revenue (US$759.6M, gives 2.5x) or 2026 revenue guidance (US$845-855M, gives about 2.2x) instead of TTM; using EV instead of equity value; confusing ACV's 8-K/earnings numbers (ACV did not mention the deal in its 10 August Q2 release). The unaffected price date (10 August) precedes media reports of a sale process (11 August).
expected_source: Copart/ACV press release 10 Sept 2026 (8-K Ex. 99.1); ACV Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 earnings press releases (8-K Ex. 99.1).
grading: Key points (all required): (1) deal terms: US$10.50 per share in cash, implied equity value about US$1.9 billion; (2) TTM revenue to 30 June 2026 = about US$801.3 million (759.6 + 418.1 - 376.4); (3) multiple about 2.37x equity value / TTM revenue (accept 2.30x-2.45x). Optional: premium about 45% to the 10 August close of US$7.26 (10.50/7.26 - 1 = 44.6%); EV-based multiple about 2.3x (equity 1,900 + debt 205 - cash 242 = about US$1.86bn). Fail if FY2025 revenue or 2026 guidance is used without computing TTM, if the answer is not a multiple, or if the deal price/equity value is wrong.
why_analysts_ask: Price-to-sales on trailing revenue is the quick yardstick for judging whether a software-enabled marketplace take-out is rich or cheap.
answer: About 2.4x: Copart's US$10.50 cash offer implies an equity value of about US$1.9 billion [W17-E1]; ACV's TTM revenue to 30 June 2026 = FY2025 US$759.6M [W17-E3] + H1 2026 US$418.1M - H1 2025 US$376.4M [W17-E2] = US$801.3M; 1,900 / 801.3 = 2.37x. question: In August 2026 SK hynix announced a share buyback. As of 3 October 2026, what is the announced size in Korean won, how many shares and what percentage of shares outstanding does it represent, and what percentage is it of the cash and cash equivalents SK hynix reported at 30 June 2026 (and of its reported net cash)?
company: SK hynix Inc. (000660.KS, Korea Exchange; not registered with the SEC; fiscal year ends December 31; reports in KRW)
failure_mode: The buyback was announced on 19 August 2026 (board decision), after the Q2 results of 28/29 July, so the cash figure must come from the Q2 2026 release (KRW 88 trillion cash and equivalents; debt KRW 18.6 trillion; net cash KRW 69.4 trillion). Traps: dollar figures (about US$28.6-29 billion) instead of won; mixing cash (88) with net cash (69.4); the share count (about 24.07 million, 3.3% of 730.5 million shares) is an estimate based on the prior close of KRW 1,662,000 and the programme is a ~3-month acquisition from 20 August; Q2 net profit (KRW 93.9 trillion) exceeded operating profit (KRW 60.5 trillion) because of KRW 63.3 trillion of investment-asset gains, so earnings are not the right denominator.
expected_source: SK hynix newsroom: 'Share Buyback and Retirement' release (19 August 2026) and '2Q26 Financial Results' (28/29 July 2026).
grading: Key points (all required): (1) buyback of KRW 40 trillion (about US$29 billion), all repurchased shares to be cancelled; about 24.07 million shares = about 3.3% of 730,492,365 shares, acquired over about three months from 20 August 2026; (2) cash and cash equivalents at 30 June 2026 = KRW 88 trillion; (3) buyback = about 45.5% of cash and cash equivalents (accept 44.5%-46.5%) and about 57.6% of net cash of KRW 69.4 trillion (accept 56.5%-58.5%). Fail if the percentage is computed on net profit, revenue or operating profit, if net cash and cash are conflated without labelling, or if the size is stated in dollars only.
why_analysts_ask: A cash-funded buyback sized against the balance sheet shows how much of the AI-memory windfall is returned to shareholders versus reinvested.
answer: KRW 40 trillion (about US$29bn), approved by the board on 19 August 2026 for about 24.07 million shares (3.3% of 730,492,365 shares at the KRW 1,662,000 prior close), all to be cancelled, acquired over about three months from 20 August [W20-E1]. Against SK hynix's Q2 2026 cash and cash equivalents of KRW 88 trillion that is 40/88 = about 45.5%; against net cash of KRW 69.4 trillion (debt KRW 18.6 trillion) it is about 57.6% [W20-E2].
